sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śalyaḥ śrutvā tu dūtānāṃ sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ abhyayāt pāṇḍavān rājan saha putrair mahārathaiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the messengers, Śalya, surrounded by a great army, advanced toward the Pāṇḍavas, O king, together with his sons, those great warriors.

sanskrit: tasya senāniveśo 'bhūd adhyardham iva yojanam tathā hi bahulāṃ senāṃ sa bibharti nararṣabhaḥ
english: His encampment extended for about one and a half yojanas, for that bull among men commanded so large an army.

sanskrit: vicitrakavacāḥ śūrā vicitradhvajakārmukāḥ vicitrābharaṇāḥ sarve vicitrarathavāhanāḥ
english: The warriors wore varied armor and bore varied banners and bows; all were adorned with varied ornaments and rode in varied chariots and vehicles.

sanskrit: svadeśaveṣābharaṇā vīrāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ tasya senāpraṇetāro babhūvuḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: Heroes clad in the dress and ornaments of their own countries, in hundreds of thousands, became the leaders of his army — those bulls among kshatriyas.

sanskrit: vyathayann iva bhūtāni kampayann iva medinīm śanair viśrāmayan senāṃ sa yayau yena pāṇḍavaḥ
english: As if distressing all creatures and making the earth tremble, he slowly rested his army and marched toward where the Pāṇḍava was.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ śrutvā mahāsenaṃ mahāratham upāyāntam abhidrutya svayam ānarca bhārata
english: Then Duryodhana, hearing that the great warrior with his great army was approaching, ran out and honoured him in person, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kārayām āsa pūjārthaṃ tasya duryodhanaḥ sabhāḥ ramaṇīyeṣu deśeṣu ratnacitrāḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: Duryodhana caused to be built for his honour rest-houses adorned with jewels and well decorated, in pleasant spots along the way.

sanskrit: sa tāḥ sabhāḥ samāsādya pūjyamāno yathāmaraḥ duryodhanasya sacivair deśe deśe yathārhataḥ ājagāma sabhām anyāṃ devāvasathavarcasam
english: Reaching those rest-houses, honoured by Duryodhana's ministers in each locality as befitted him — like a god — he came at last to another hall that shone like a divine abode.

sanskrit: sa tatra viṣayair yuktaḥ kalyāṇair atimānuṣaiḥ mene 'bhyadhikam ātmānam avamene puraṃdaram
english: There, surrounded by auspicious pleasures beyond human measure, he thought himself superior to all and held even Indra the destroyer of cities in contempt.

sanskrit: papraccha sa tataḥ preṣyān prahṛṣṭaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ yudhiṣṭhirasya puruṣāḥ ke nu cakruḥ sabhā imāḥ ānīyantāṃ sabhākārāḥ pradeyārhā hi me matāḥ
english: Delighted, that bull among kshatriyas then asked his attendants: 'Who are the men of Yudhiṣṭhira who built these halls? Let the builders be brought here; they deserve gifts from me, I think.'

sanskrit: gūḍho duryodhanas tatra darśayām āsa mātulam taṃ dṛṣṭvā madrarājas tu jñātvā yatnaṃ ca tasya tam pariṣvajyābravīt prīta iṣṭo 'rtho gṛhyatām iti
english: There Duryodhana, who had kept himself hidden, revealed himself to his maternal uncle. On seeing him, the king of Madra understood the effort he had made, and embracing him with affection, said: 'Excellent! Choose any boon you wish.'

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca satyavāg bhava kalyāṇa varo vai mama dīyatām sarvasenāpraṇetā me bhavān bhavitum arhati
english: Duryodhana said: Be true to your word, O auspicious one, and grant me this boon: you should become the commander-in-chief of all my armies.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kṛtam ity abravīc chalyaḥ kim anyat kriyatām iti kṛtam ity eva gāndhāriḥ pratyuvāca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Śalya replied 'Done!' and said, 'What else shall I do?' And the son of Gāndhārī replied again and again, 'It is done, it is done!'

sanskrit: sa tathā śalyam āmantrya punar āyāt svakaṃ puram śalyo jagāma kaunteyān ākhyātuṃ karma tasya tat
english: Having thus taken leave of Śalya, he returned to his own city. Śalya went to the sons of Kuntī to inform them of this event.

sanskrit: upaplavyaṃ sa gatvā tu skandhāvāraṃ praviśya ca pāṇḍavān atha tān sarvāñ śalyas tatra dadarśa ha
english: Going to Upaplavya and entering the encampment, Śalya saw all the Pāṇḍavas assembled there.

sanskrit: sametya tu mahābāhuḥ śalyaḥ pāṇḍusutais tadā pādyam arghyaṃ ca gāṃ caiva pratyagṛhṇād yathāvidhi
english: Meeting with the sons of Pāṇḍu, the mighty-armed Śalya received water for his feet, the honour-gift, and the cow, all according to proper rite.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuśalapūrvaṃ sa madrarājo 'risūdanaḥ prītyā paramayā yuktaḥ samāśliṣya yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Then the king of Madra, that destroyer of foes, filled with the greatest affection, first exchanged words of welcome and embraced Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tathā bhīmārjunau hṛṣṭau svasrīyau ca yamāv ubhau āsane copaviṣṭas tu śalyaḥ pārtham uvāca ha
english: Likewise he greeted the joyful Bhīma and Arjuna, and both of his sister's sons, the twins. Then, seated on a seat, Śalya spoke to the son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: kuśalaṃ rājaśārdūla kaccit te kurunandana araṇyavāsād diṣṭyāsi vimukto jayatāṃ vara
english: Are you well, O tiger among kings, O joy of the Kurus? By good fortune you are freed from your forest exile, O foremost among the victorious!

sanskrit: suduṣkaraṃ kṛtaṃ rājan nirjane vasatā vane bhrātṛbhiḥ saha rājendra kṛṣṇayā cānayā saha
english: A very difficult thing has been accomplished, O king — dwelling in the uninhabited forest together with your brothers and with this Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī), O lord of kings.

sanskrit: ajñātavāsaṃ ghoraṃ ca vasatā duṣkaraṃ kṛtam duḥkham eva kutaḥ saukhyaṃ rājyabhraṣṭasya bhārata
english: The terrible year of incognito living was also endured with difficulty. Where indeed is happiness for one bereft of his kingdom? Only suffering, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: duḥkhasyaitasya mahato dhārtarāṣṭrakṛtasya vai avāpsyasi sukhaṃ rājan hatvā śatrūn paraṃtapa
english: From this great sorrow caused by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, you shall attain happiness, O king, having slain your enemies, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: viditaṃ te mahārāja lokatattvaṃ narādhipa tasmāl lobhakṛtaṃ kiṃ cit tava tāta na vidyate
english: The truth of the world is known to you, O great king, O lord of men; therefore, my dear, nothing caused by greed is found in you.

sanskrit: tato 'syākathayad rājā duryodhanasamāgamam tac ca śuśrūṣitaṃ sarvaṃ varadānaṃ ca bhārata
english: Then the king told him of his encounter with Duryodhana — all the hospitable service he had received and the granting of the boon, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sukṛtaṃ te kṛtaṃ rājan prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā duryodhanasya yad vīra tvayā vācā pratiśrutam ekaṃ tv icchāmi bhadraṃ te kriyamāṇaṃ mahīpate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Well done, O king! What you, O hero, promised by word to Duryodhana was done with a rejoicing heart. Yet one thing I wish to be done, may it go well with you, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: bhavān iha mahārāja vāsudevasamo yudhi karṇārjunābhyāṃ saṃprāpte dvairathe rājasattama karṇasya bhavatā kāryaṃ sārathyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: You, O great king, are the equal of Vāsudeva in battle. When the single combat between Karṇa and Arjuna takes place, O foremost of kings, you should act as charioteer for Karṇa — there is no doubt about this.

sanskrit: tatra pālyo 'rjuno rājan yadi matpriyam icchasi tejovadhaś ca te kāryaḥ sauter asmajjayāvahaḥ akartavyam api hy etat kartum arhasi mātula
english: In that situation Arjuna is to be protected, O king, if you wish what is dear to me. And you must also undermine the spirit of the son of the charioteer, bringing victory to our side. Though this is improper, you should do it, O uncle.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca śṛṇu pāṇḍava bhadraṃ te yad bravīṣi durātmanaḥ tejovadhanimittaṃ māṃ sūtaputrasya saṃyuge
english: Śalya said: Hear me, O Pāṇḍava, may it go well with you! You speak of me as one who will crush the spirit of that wicked-souled son of the charioteer in battle.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tasya bhaviṣyāmi saṃgrāme sārathir dhruvam vāsudevena hi samaṃ nityaṃ māṃ sa hi manyate
english: I shall certainly be his charioteer in battle. For he always considers me the equal of Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ kuruśārdūla pratīpam ahitaṃ vacaḥ dhruvaṃ saṃkathayiṣyāmi yoddhukāmasya saṃyuge
english: To him, when he desires to fight in battle, I shall certainly speak discouraging and harmful words, O tiger of the Kurus.

sanskrit: yathā sa hṛtadarpaś ca hṛtatejāś ca pāṇḍava bhaviṣyati sukhaṃ hantuṃ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: So that he will become robbed of his pride and robbed of his spirit, O Pāṇḍava, and easily slain — this I tell you truly.

sanskrit: evam etat kariṣyāmi yathā tāta tvam āttha mām yac cānyad api śakṣyāmi tat kariṣyāmi te priyam
english: I shall do this exactly as you have told me, my dear. And whatever else I am able to do, I shall do what is pleasing to you.

sanskrit: yac ca duḥkhaṃ tvayā prāptaṃ dyūte vai kṛṣṇayā saha paruṣāṇi ca vākyāni sūtaputrakṛtāni vai
english: The suffering that was inflicted on you at the dice game together with Kṛṣṇā, and the harsh words spoken by the son of the charioteer —

sanskrit: jaṭāsurāt parikleśaḥ kīcakāc ca mahādyute draupadyādhigataṃ sarvaṃ damayantyā yathāśubham
english: The affliction from Jaṭāsura, and from Kīcaka — all that was obtained by Draupadī, O greatly resplendent one, just as Damayantī suffered misfortune —

sanskrit: sarvaṃ duḥkham idaṃ vīra sukhodarkaṃ bhaviṣyati nātra manyus tvayā kāryo vidhir hi balavattaraḥ
english: All this suffering, O hero, shall bear fruit as happiness. You must not be angry about this, for fate is more powerful.

sanskrit: duḥkhāni hi mahātmānaḥ prāpnuvanti yudhiṣṭhira devair api hi duḥkhāni prāptāni jagatīpate
english: For great souls encounter sufferings, O Yudhiṣṭhira; even by the gods have sufferings been encountered, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: indreṇa śrūyate rājan sabhāryeṇa mahātmanā anubhūtaṃ mahad duḥkhaṃ devarājena bhārata
english: It is heard, O king, that Indra, together with his wife, that great soul, the king of the gods, experienced great suffering, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca katham indreṇa rājendra sabhāryeṇa mahātmanā duḥkhaṃ prāptaṃ paraṃ ghoram etad icchāmi veditum
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How did Indra, together with his wife, that great soul, O king of kings, come to experience extreme and terrible suffering? I wish to know this.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca śṛṇu rājan purā vṛttam itihāsaṃ purātanam sabhāryeṇa yathā prāptaṃ duḥkham indreṇa bhārata
english: Śalya said: Hear, O king, this ancient history of former times — how Indra together with his wife came to experience suffering, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā prajāpatir hy āsīd devaśreṣṭho mahātapāḥ sa putraṃ vai triśirasam indradrohāt kilāsṛjat
english: Tvaṣṭṛ was a lord of creatures (Prajāpati), the foremost of the gods, of great austerity. He created a son named Triśiras (Three-headed) out of enmity toward Indra.

sanskrit: aindraṃ sa prārthayat sthānaṃ viśvarūpo mahādyutiḥ tais tribhir vadanair ghoraiḥ sūryendujvalanopamaiḥ
english: He, Viśvarūpa of great brilliance, coveted the station of Indra, with his three terrible faces blazing like the sun, fire, and lightning.

sanskrit: vedān ekena so 'dhīte surām ekena cāpibat ekena ca diśaḥ sarvāḥ pibann iva nirīkṣate
english: With one mouth he studied the Vedas; with another he drank Sura (liquor); and with the third he gazed upon all the directions as if drinking them in.

sanskrit: sa tapasvī mṛdur dānto dharme tapasi codyataḥ tapo 'tapyan mahat tīvraṃ suduścaram ariṃdama
english: This ascetic was gentle and self-controlled, devoted to duty and austerity; he performed great and severe austerities that were very hard to undertake, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: tasya dṛṣṭvā tapovīryaṃ sattvaṃ cāmitatejasaḥ viṣādam agamac chakra indro 'yaṃ mā bhaved iti
english: Seeing the power of his asceticism and the might of one of immeasurable brilliance, Śakra fell into anxiety, thinking: 'May this one not become Indra.'

sanskrit: kathaṃ sajjeta bhogeṣu na ca tapyen mahat tapaḥ vivardhamānas triśirāḥ sarvaṃ tribhuvanaṃ graset
english: 'How can he be made to attach himself to pleasures and not perform great austerity? As Triśiras grows, he might devour all three worlds.'

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya bahudhā buddhimān bharatarṣabha ājñāpayat so 'psarasas tvaṣṭṛputrapralobhane
english: Thinking in many ways, that wise one, O bull of the Bhāratas, commanded the apsaras (celestial nymphs) to go and tempt the son of Tvaṣṭṛ.

sanskrit: yathā sa sajjet triśirāḥ kāmabhogeṣu vai bhṛśam kṣipraṃ kuruta gacchadhvaṃ pralobhayata māciram
english: 'So that Triśiras may be deeply attached to the pleasures of desire, quickly do this, go forth, seduce him — do not delay!'

sanskrit: śṛṅgāraveṣāḥ suśroṇyo bhāvair yuktā manoharaiḥ pralobhayata bhadraṃ vaḥ śamayadhvaṃ bhayaṃ mama
english: 'Adorned in amorous dress, O fair-hipped ones, equipped with enchanting ways, seduce him — may it go well with you! Dispel my fear.'

sanskrit: asvasthaṃ hy ātmanātmānaṃ lakṣayāmi varāṅganāḥ bhayam etan mahāghoraṃ kṣipraṃ nāśayatābalāḥ
english: 'For I perceive that I am not at ease within myself, O lovely women. Quickly destroy this great and terrible fear, O you gentle ones.'

sanskrit: apsarasa ūcuḥ tathā yatnaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ śakra tasya pralobhane yathā nāvāpsyasi bhayaṃ tasmād balaniṣūdana
english: The apsaras said: We shall make such effort to seduce him, O Śakra, that you will no longer feel fear from him, O destroyer of Bala.

sanskrit: nirdahann iva cakṣurbhyāṃ yo 'sāv āste taponidhiḥ taṃ pralobhayituṃ deva gacchāmaḥ sahitā vayam yatiṣyāmo vaśe kartuṃ vyapanetuṃ ca te bhayam
english: That treasure of austerity who sits as if burning everything with his eyes — to seduce him, O god, we go together; we shall strive to bring him under control and to remove your fear.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca indreṇa tās tv anujñātā jagmus triśiraso 'ntikam tatra tā vividhair bhāvair lobhayantyo varāṅganāḥ nṛtyaṃ saṃdarśayantyaś ca tathaivāṅgeṣu sauṣṭhavam
english: Śalya said: Permitted by Indra, they went to the presence of Triśiras. There those lovely women tried to seduce him with various moods, displaying their dancing and likewise the grace of their limbs.

sanskrit: viceruḥ saṃpraharṣaṃ ca nābhyagacchan mahātapāḥ indriyāṇi vaśe kṛtvā pūrṇasāgarasaṃnibhaḥ
english: They roamed about delightfully, yet they did not reach him — the great ascetic, having subdued his senses, was like a full ocean (unagitated).

sanskrit: tās tu yatnaṃ paraṃ kṛtvā punaḥ śakram upasthitāḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ sarvā devarājam athābruvan
english: Having made their utmost effort, they returned to Śakra; and all of them, with palms joined, spoke then to the king of the gods.

sanskrit: na sa śakyaḥ sudurdharṣo dhairyāc cālayituṃ prabho yat te kāryaṃ mahābhāga kriyatāṃ tadanantaram
english: He is not capable of being moved from his steadfastness, O lord — he is very difficult to assail. Whatever is your purpose, O greatly fortunate one, let that be done next.

sanskrit: saṃpūjyāpsarasaḥ śakro visṛjya ca mahāmatiḥ cintayām āsa tasyaiva vadhopāyaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Śakra, that great-minded one, honoured the apsaras and dismissed them, and then began to contemplate a means of slaying that great soul.

sanskrit: sa tūṣṇīṃ cintayan vīro devarājaḥ pratāpavān viniścitamatir dhīmān vadhe triśiraso 'bhavat
english: That hero, the powerful king of the gods, deliberating in silence, the wise one with mind made up, decided on the slaying of Triśiras.

sanskrit: vajram asya kṣipāmy adya sa kṣipraṃ na bhaviṣyati śatruḥ pravṛddho nopekṣyo durbalo 'pi balīyasā
english: 'I shall hurl my thunderbolt at him today; he will quickly cease to be. An enemy grown powerful must not be ignored, even by the strong, even if he be weak.'

sanskrit: śāstrabuddhyā viniścitya kṛtvā buddhiṃ vadhe dṛḍhām atha vaiśvānaranibhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayāvaham mumoca vajraṃ saṃkruddhaḥ śakras triśirasaṃ prati
english: Having determined this with the reasoning of scripture and having firmly made up his mind to slay, Śakra, enraged, then hurled the thunderbolt — resembling fire, of terrible form, inspiring fear — at Triśiras.

sanskrit: sa papāta hatas tena vajreṇa dṛḍham āhataḥ parvatasyeva śikharaṃ praṇunnaṃ medinītale
english: He fell, slain, struck hard by that thunderbolt, like the peak of a mountain shattered to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: taṃ tu vajrahataṃ dṛṣṭvā śayānam acalopamam na śarma lebhe devendro dīpitas tasya tejasā hato 'pi dīptatejāḥ sa jīvann iva ca dṛśyate
english: But seeing him struck by the thunderbolt and lying motionless like a mountain, the lord of the gods found no comfort, being scorched by his brilliance; even slain, he blazed with radiance and appeared as if still alive.

sanskrit: abhitas tatra takṣāṇaṃ ghaṭamānaṃ śacīpatiḥ apaśyad abravīc cainaṃ satvaraṃ pākaśāsanaḥ kṣipraṃ chindhi śirāṃsy asya kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama
english: There the lord of Śacī (Indra, Pākaśāsana) saw a carpenter at work nearby and hastily said to him: 'Quickly cut off his heads! Do my bidding.'

sanskrit: takṣovāca mahāskandho bhṛśaṃ hy eṣa paraśur na tariṣyati kartuṃ cāhaṃ na śakṣyāmi karma sadbhir vigarhitam
english: The carpenter said: This axe is very large — it will not succeed (in cutting through his great trunk). And I am not able to perform a deed censured by the good.

sanskrit: indra uvāca mā bhais tvaṃ kṣipram etad vai kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama matprasādād dhi te śastraṃ vajrakalpaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Indra said: Do not be afraid; quickly do my bidding. By my favour your tool shall become equal to the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: takṣovāca kaṃ bhavantam ahaṃ vidyāṃ ghorakarmāṇam adya vai etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tattvena kathayasva me
english: The carpenter said: Whom should I know you to be — you who would have me do this terrible deed today? I wish to hear this truly; tell me in truth.

sanskrit: indra uvāca aham indro devarājas takṣan viditam astu te kuruṣvaitad yathoktaṃ me takṣan mā tvaṃ vicāraya
english: Indra said: I am Indra, the king of the gods, O carpenter — let this be known to you. Do exactly as I have told you, O carpenter; do not deliberate.

sanskrit: takṣovāca krūreṇa nāpatrapase kathaṃ śakreha karmaṇā ṛṣiputram imaṃ hatvā brahmahatyābhayaṃ na te
english: The carpenter said: Are you not ashamed of this cruel deed, O Śakra? Having slain this son of a rishi, do you not fear the sin of brahmin-slaughter?

sanskrit: indra uvāca paścād dharmaṃ cariṣyāmi pāvanārthaṃ suduścaram śatrur eṣa mahāvīryo vajreṇa nihato mayā
english: Indra said: Afterwards I shall undertake the very difficult dharmic practices for purification. This enemy was of great power; he has been struck down by my thunderbolt.

sanskrit: adyāpi cāham udvignas takṣann asmād bibhemi vai kṣipraṃ chindhi śirāṃsi tvaṃ kariṣye 'nugrahaṃ tava
english: Even now I am troubled, O carpenter, and I fear him. Quickly cut off his heads; I shall bestow a favour upon you.

sanskrit: śiraḥ paśos te dāsyanti bhāgaṃ yajñeṣu mānavāḥ eṣa te 'nugrahas takṣan kṣipraṃ kuru mama priyam
english: Men will give you the heads of animals as your share in sacrifices — this is your favour, O carpenter. Quickly do what pleases me.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca etac chrutvā tu takṣā sa mahendravacanaṃ tadā śirāṃsy atha triśirasaḥ kuṭhāreṇācchinat tadā
english: Śalya said: Having heard that speech of the great Indra, the carpenter then cut off the heads of Triśiras with his axe.

sanskrit: nikṛtteṣu tatas teṣu niṣkrāmaṃs triśirās tv atha kapiñjalās tittirāś ca kalaviṅkāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: When those heads were severed, from Triśiras as he lay came forth partridges, francolin-partridges (tittira), and sparrows (kalavinka) on all sides.

sanskrit: yena vedān adhīte sma pibate somam eva ca tasmād vaktrān viniṣpetuḥ kṣipraṃ tasya kapiñjalāḥ
english: From the mouth with which he had studied the Vedas and also drunk Soma, kapiñjala birds quickly flew forth.

sanskrit: yena sarvā diśo rājan pibann iva nirīkṣate tasmād vaktrād viniṣpetus tittirās tasya pāṇḍava
english: From the mouth with which he had gazed upon all directions as if drinking them in, O king, tittira birds flew forth from his mouth, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: yat surāpaṃ tu tasyāsīd vaktraṃ triśirasas tadā kalaviṅkā viniṣpetus tenāsya bharatarṣabha
english: And from the mouth of Triśiras that had drunk liquor, kalaviṅka (sparrow) birds flew forth, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tatas teṣu nikṛtteṣu vijvaro maghavān abhūt jagāma tridivaṃ hṛṣṭas takṣāpi svagṛhān yayau
english: Then, with those heads cut off, Maghavan (Indra) was free from fever and went joyfully to the three heavens; the carpenter too went to his own home.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā prajāpatiḥ śrutvā śakreṇātha hataṃ sutam krodhasaṃraktanayana idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Tvaṣṭṛ the Prajāpati, hearing that his son had been slain by Śakra, with eyes reddened by rage, spoke these words:

sanskrit: tapyamānaṃ tapo nityaṃ kṣāntaṃ dāntaṃ jitendriyam anāparādhinaṃ yasmāt putraṃ hiṃsitavān mama
english: 'Because you have slain my son — ever performing austerity, patient, self-controlled, with conquered senses, blameless —

sanskrit: tasmāc chakravadhārthāya vṛtram utpādayāmy aham lokāḥ paśyantu me vīryaṃ tapasaś ca balaṃ mahat sa ca paśyatu devendro durātmā pāpacetanaḥ
english: Therefore I shall create Vṛtra for the purpose of slaying Śakra! Let the worlds behold my might and the great power of my austerity — and let that wicked-minded, evil-hearted lord of the gods behold it too!'

sanskrit: upaspṛśya tataḥ kruddhas tapasvī sumahāyaśāḥ agniṃ hutvā samutpādya ghoraṃ vṛtram uvāca ha indraśatro vivardhasva prabhāvāt tapaso mama
english: Then that ascetic of very great renown, enraged, sipped water for purification and offered oblations into the fire. He created the terrible Vṛtra and said: 'O enemy of Indra, grow mighty through the power of my austerity!'
